questions.text: A binary search tree T contains n distinct elements. What is the time complexity of picking an element in T that is smaller than the maximum element in T?
questions.solution:
Look only at the root and its children:
- If the root has a right child, the root is smaller than something, so it is not the maximum [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] pick the root.
- Otherwise the root is the maximum, and its left child is smaller [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] pick the left child.

A constant number of steps [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]\Theta(1)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(1)[/latex]

questions.text: Let P be an array containing n integers. Let t be the lowest upper bound on the number of comparisons of the array elements, required to find the minimum and maximum values in an arbitrary array of n elements. Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.solution:
Process elements in pairs: compare the two, then compare the smaller with the current min and the larger with the current max. That is 3 comparisons per 2 elements: about [latex]\lceil3n/2\rceil-2[/latex] comparisons, and this is optimal.

So [latex]t \gt n[/latex] and [latex]t\le3\lceil n/2\rceil[/latex].

Answer: [latex]t \gt n[/latex] and [latex]t\le3\lceil\frac n2\rceil[/latex]

questions.text:
A stack is implemented with an array of [latex]{ }^{\prime} A[0 \ldots N-1]^{\prime}[/latex] and a variable [latex]\text { 'pos'. }[/latex] The push and pop operations are defined by the following code.
 push (x)
    A[pos] <- x
    pos <- pos -1
end push
pop()
    pos <- pos+1
    return A[pos]
end pop

Which of the following will initialize an empty stack with capacity N for the above implementation?
questions.solution:
push writes at A[pos] and then decrements pos, so the stack grows downward from the top of the array. pop first increments pos and then reads.

For an empty stack with room for N elements, pos must start at the last index: pos [latex]\leftarrow[/latex] N [latex]-[/latex] 1.

Answer: pos [latex]\leftarrow[/latex] N-1

questions.text: Of the following, which best approximates the ratio of the number of nonterminal nodes in the total number of nodes in a complete K-ary tree of depth N ?
questions.solution:
In a complete K-ary tree, each level has K times the nodes of the level above, so the leaves are about [latex]\frac{K-1}{K}[/latex] of all nodes. The internal (non-terminal) nodes are [latex]\frac{K^N-1}{K-1}[/latex] out of [latex]\frac{K^{N+1}-1}{K-1}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ratio [latex]\approx\frac1K[/latex].

Answer: 1/K

questions.text: If an array A contains the items 10, 4, 7, 23, 67, 12 and 5 in that order, what will be the resultant array A after third pass of insertion sort?
questions.solution:
Insertion sort, inserting one element per pass:
- Pass 1 (insert 4): 4, 10, 7, 23, 67, 12, 5
- Pass 2 (insert 7): 4, 7, 10, 23, 67, 12, 5
- Pass 3 (insert 23): already in place [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4, 7, 10, 23, 67, 12, 5

Answer: 4, 7, 10, 23, 67, 12, 5
